title: Best Beaches & Beachfront Apartments in Supetar 2027
metaDescription: Supetar's best beaches: Banj, Vela Luka, Tri Mosta, Vlačica and Acapulco. Beach types, distances and beachfront apartment prices from about €70 a night.
content:
## Best Beaches in Supetar

Supetar sits on the north coast of Brač, directly opposite Split. Most of its beaches are pebble or concrete-slab beaches with clear water. Two have sandy seabed, which is rare in Dalmatia. All are free to enter. Sun loungers and umbrellas are rented at the busier beaches.

### Vela Luka Beach: best for small children

Vela Luka is about 2 km from the town center. It is made up of two coves, Vela Luka and Mala Luka. It has pebble and concrete sections on land and fine sand in the water. The water is shallow, which suits toddlers and non-swimmers. Nearby are restaurants, water sports rentals and sunbeds. Bili Rat, next to it, is another quiet option.

### Banj Beach: best for families who want activities

Banj is the oldest beach in Supetar and sits about 15 minutes on foot from the center, west of the port. The shore is pebbles and concrete slabs, and the seabed turns to sand after a few meters. A pine forest gives natural shade, and the bay is sheltered from wind, so the sea stays calm. The beach has a water slide, a small water park, pedal boats, a volleyball court, showers and beach massage tents. Parking near the beach is limited.

### Tri Mosta (Three Bridges): best near the hotel area

Tri Mosta is a pebble beach with concrete terraces and gravel entry points. It is the main beach of the hotel area north of town and has no dedicated parking. Shade comes from trees behind the terraces.

### Vlačica and Acapulco: best for a short swim

Vlačica is a small pebble and rocky beach west of the ferry dock with natural shade and several cafés. Acapulco is a pebble beach in the very center, a few minutes from the ferry port. It suits a quick swim before a ferry or after dinner.

### Vrilo Beach: best for shade

Vrilo is a long pebble beach backed by a pine forest. It works well in July and August when open concrete terraces get too hot by noon.

## Which Supetar Beach Is Best for You?

| Need | Best choice |
|---|---|
| Toddlers, shallow sand | Vela Luka |
| Slides, pedal boats, activities | Banj |
| Hotel-area terraces | Tri Mosta |
| Shade in midsummer | Vrilo or Banj |
| Closest to the ferry | Acapulco |

Banj gets the most attention in guides, but Vela Luka is the better beach. It has real sand, shallower water and fewer people. Banj is better only when children want a water park.

## Beachfront Apartments in Supetar

Supetar has a large supply of private apartments. Most are small family-run buildings with 1 to 3 bedrooms, air conditioning, a balcony and a kitchen. Many sit 50 to 150 m from the sea.

### Typical prices

- **Budget (€45–€80 per night):** Studios and one-bedroom units 100 m from the sea, usually without a pool. These prices are common in May, June and September.
- **Mid-range (€90–€150 per night):** Sea-view apartments with parking, a terrace and a walk of under 5 minutes to a beach. Apartment Star is listed as beachfront with free private parking and a 9.1/10 guest score.
- **Premium (€250+ per night):** Large sea-view apartments such as Daphne Luxe Retreat, a 4-minute walk from Vrilo Beach.

Prices in July and August are typically 40–70% higher than in May or late September.

### Best areas to stay

- **Town center and harbor:** Walkable to Acapulco and Vlačica, plus restaurants and the ferry. It is noisier in the evening.
- **Banj and Vlačica side (west):** Quieter, with pine shade and Banj close by. Apartments Derado and Vila Magdalena are in this part of town.
- **Tri Mosta and hotel area (north):** Flat coastal walks and larger resort infrastructure.
- **Vela Luka (about 2 km):** Best for families who want sand. Some family apartments with pools are a 5-minute walk from the beach.

## Getting to Supetar

Car ferries from Split take about 50 minutes, and services run through the day all year round. Supetar is the main ferry port on Brač, so the island's buses start here. Buses and taxis reach Bol (about 40 km away) and Zlatni Rat. Bring a car only if you plan to explore the island. For a beach stay in Supetar, walking is enough.

## Local Tips

- Book beachfront apartments for July and August by March or April. The best units near Banj and Vela Luka go first.
- Choose an apartment with air conditioning and a parking space. Parking near Banj and Tri Mosta is limited.
- Take water shoes. Pebbles and concrete edges are hard on bare feet.
- Swim early at Banj, before 10:00, to avoid the slide queues.
- For a quiet evening swim, use Vlačica or Acapulco, which are walkable from the harbor.
- A day trip to Zlatni Rat in Bol is worth doing once. Do not spend the whole stay there, since Supetar's beaches are close and free.

## Best Time to Visit

Sea temperatures reach about 24–26 °C in July and August. June and September offer water around 22–24 °C, lower prices and fewer people. Many beach bars and rentals close by mid-October.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Supetar?
faq.answer: Vela Luka is the best all-round beach in Supetar. It has sandy seabed, shallow water and sits about 2 km from the center. Banj is the better choice if you want a water park and pedal boats.

faq.question: Are Supetar beaches sandy or pebbly?
faq.answer: Most are pebble or concrete-slab beaches. Banj has a sandy seabed after a few meters, and Vela Luka has sand in the water. Acapulco, Tri Mosta and Vlačica are pebble.

faq.question: How much does a beachfront apartment in Supetar cost?
faq.answer: Simple apartments near the sea start around €45–€80 per night in the shoulder season. Sea-view and beachfront units usually cost €100–€150, and premium apartments reach about €300. Summer peak prices run 40–70% higher.

faq.question: How far is Banj Beach from the center of Supetar?
faq.answer: Banj is about a 15-minute walk from the town center. It lies west of the ferry port. Parking near the beach is limited.

faq.question: Is Supetar good for a beach holiday with children?
faq.answer: Yes. Vela Luka has shallow sandy water, and Banj has a water slide, water park and calm, wind-protected sea. Many apartments are within a 5-minute walk of these beaches.

faq.question: How do you get from Split to Supetar?
faq.answer: Take a car or passenger ferry from Split to Supetar. The crossing takes about 50 minutes. Crossings run through the day all year round, with more departures in summer.

quickAnswer: The best beaches in Supetar are Vela Luka (sandy, shallow, 2 km from town), Banj (sand-and-pebble, 15 minutes on foot, with a water park), Tri Mosta (pebble, by the hotel area) and central Acapulco. Beachfront apartments start around €70 per night outside peak season and rise to €300 for premium sea-view units.
